raw:
Both modules appear to encode the same rules, just in a different order and with different predicate names. Module B also seems to contain every clause that A does.

Checking for omissions in B:
- Sensitive areas: law_enforcement, migration, asylum and border_control_management are all present.
- Member points: 1, 6 and 7 are all present.
- Registration articles: paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 are all present.
- Excluded Annex VIII points: 6, 8 and 9 are all present.
- Annex IX points: 1, 2, 3 and 5 are all present.
- Letter (b) items: points 1 to 5, 8 and 9 are all present.
- Letter (c) and letter (a) items are present.
- Restricted-section access: both the Commission and the Article 74(8) authorities are present.

The two modules therefore agree on every sentence. Neither captures sentence 1 fully, because the "shall include only" restriction relies on an applicable_information fact that the text does not state. Sentences 2 to 5 are partial on both sides for the same reason: they carry the item lists but add the applicability condition. Sentence 6 is full on both sides, though the access restriction is expressed only as permission rules.

Sentence 1 is partial on both sides, because the registration requirement and the secure section are present but the "only" restriction is expressed through the extra applicability condition.
